description.en: The short version, built for travellers arriving on the morning train and leaving at night. It covers the three sights nobody should miss and leaves an hour at the end for the square after dark.

notes.en: Buy the Registan ticket first thing — the queue doubles after ten. Lunch is easiest near the bazaar.

note.en: Finish with the Registan again after sunset; the illuminated facades are a different building.

description.en: The pace most people want. Day one is the Timurid core in the centre; day two moves out to the observatory and the paper mill, with room for a long lunch.

notes.en: Day two needs a car or taxi for two short hops. Both stops are on the same side of the city.

note.en: All within walking distance of each other.
Start at Shah-i-Zinda by eight to have the lane to yourself.

title: Samarkand in Three Days
description: For travellers who want to stop rushing. Everything in the two-day itinerary, spread out, with a third day for the workshops, the bazaar at its own pace, and a second visit to whichever site you liked most.
notes: The third day is deliberately light. A day trip to Shahrisabz over the mountain pass can replace it if you would rather cover ground.

days.title: The Registan and around
days.note: A half day, so you can arrive on the midday train and still do it.

days.title: Tombs and the great mosque
days.note: The bazaar sits between the other two — use it as your lunch stop.

days.title: Out of the centre
days.note: Half a day of driving and craft workshops, back in town for the evening.

description.en: Bukhara rewards walking more than any other city here. Two days is enough to cover the monuments without ever needing a taxi, and to end both evenings at the pool.

notes.en: Almost everything is inside a twenty-minute walk of Lyab-i Hauz. Wear shoes you can cover ten kilometres in.

note.en: Save Poi Kalyan for late afternoon when the brick turns gold.

description.en: One day inside the walls covers the monuments; the second is for the parts of Khiva that only appear when the day-trippers leave. Staying overnight inside Ichan Kala is the whole difference.

notes.en: A single combined ticket covers most sites inside the walls and is valid for two days.

note.en: Climb the Kunya-Ark watchtower early to get the layout in your head.

description.en: Designed for the day you land or the day before you fly home. Old town in the morning, metro in the middle, modern city in the evening — all reachable without a car.

notes.en: Metro tickets are a flat fare and the trains run every few minutes. Keep some cash for the bazaar.

note.en: Chorsu and Hazrati Imam are a short walk apart; take the metro east from there.
